applicability: code-reviewer failure_scenario emission and builder-agent review-feedback handling; observed once at scale (5 findings in one round), single-occurrence so not yet recurrence.

evidence.source_reference: Issue #73 / #77 field report — Ansible estate tranche-1 run, 2026-08-03; third deep-review round

expected_behavior: A builder acting on review feedback that carries a concrete repro runs that repro before implementing, and reports the delta when the stated trigger does not reproduce, rather than inheriting the rationale. A reviewer emitting a failure scenario labels it measured or reasoned, mirroring the fleet's existing verified/sourced/unverified evidence discipline, so a consumer can tell which scenarios were executed.
observation: A reviewer-supplied failure repro was accepted as the stated cause in 3 of 5 findings from one deep-review round, but running each repro showed the stated trigger did not reproduce while a narrower one did. The underlying defects were real in all three cases, so the findings were useful; the supplied rationale was not. Examples: a claim that a censored assert means fail_msg never reaches the operator (it does, via the error banner); a claim of two ConfigParser triggers where neither fires (interpolation is lazy per-key, and CPython auto-enables UTF-8 mode under LC_ALL=C); a claim that a document undercounted at two where the derived count was five across four roles.
reason: Builder-consuming half already owned verbatim at sde-fullstack.md:108. Reviewer-emitting half exists only for security findings at code-reviewer.md:55. Fleet reviewers cannot execute code per code-reviewer.md:128, so the residue is traced-and-confirmed-by-reading versus assumed-runtime-semantics, not measured versus reasoned. Recurrence 1.
